report.source_text: After the opening of the abdominal cavity, the tumor wall was incised, and 100 L of fluid was aspirated. Because of its enormous size, the neoplasm could not be weighed after the removal. However, since approximately 100 L of clear, colorless fluid had been drained, it is safe to estimate the tumor mass to be around 100 kg. The abdominal cavity was then inspected, and the adhesions of the tumor wall with the parietal peritoneum and abdominal organs were released. During the operation, it became apparent that the tumor originated from the left ovary. In the next stage, the abdominal and pelvic organs were inspected. The right ovary, right fallopian tube, and uterus were normal, as were other abdominal organs. The tumor wall was then removed along with part of the left ovary. The specimen was sent for a frozen section procedure.

report.source_text: After the fixation of the cyst in 10% neutral buffered formalin, numerous sections of the tumor were cut for paraffin blocks, and the definitive histopathological diagnosis was serous cystadenofibroma of the ovary (ICD-O 9014/0). The differences between the intraoperative examination report and the formalin-fixed material result from the fact that multiple samples were taken, not just one as during the frozen section. The differentiating factor is the more prominent stromal component present in the formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded samples. Nonetheless, this did not change the clinical management of our patient.

report.source_text: In the postoperative period, the patient was under the care of rehabilitation specialists who helped her to recover quickly and improve her physical fitness. The patient started walking the day after the procedure with the help of physiotherapists. The Foley catheter was removed on the second day after surgery. The patient was discharged from the hospital in good condition on the seventh postoperative day. The patient returned to the local clinic 2 weeks after the surgery to have the stitches removed. The patient felt good, the symptoms subsided, she breathed easily and moved efficiently.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old woman with a history of childhood obesity presented with massive abdominal enlargement (circumference 195 cm), left-sided periodic abdominal pain, scanty and irregular menses (up to 37 days), and infertility. On admission, she was afebrile and in moderately good general condition. Abdominal and pelvic ultrasound revealed a massive fluid-filled tumor mass with segmental solid components; however, the tumor's origin could not be reliably identified due to the patient's large abdominal size, with the ultrasound transducer visualizing only 24-25 cm of the neoplasm. Surgical exploration confirmed the tumor originated from the left ovary. Intraoperatively, 100 liters of clear, colorless fluid was aspirated, with the tumor mass estimated at approximately 100 kg. The right ovary, fallopian tube, uterus, and other abdominal organs were normal. The tumor wall was removed along with part of the left ovary. Histopathological examination of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue confirmed the definitive diagnosis of serous cystadenofibroma of the ovary (ICD-O 9014/0), characterized by a prominent stromal component. The patient recovered well postoperatively with multidisciplinary rehabilitation support, was discharged on postoperative day 7 in good condition, and reported symptom resolution with improved mobility and breathing at 2-week follow-up.
